law_name: Constitutional revision deconstitutionalising the appointment of King's commissioners and mayors (initiative bill Jetten, 34.716)
description: Second-reading constitutional bill introduced by Jetten in 2017 as a backbench MP, removing from the Constitution the rule that mayors and King's commissioners are appointed by the Crown, so that the method of appointment can be set by ordinary law. Adopted by the House in January 2018 and, according to Parlement.com, by the Senate in November 2018.
significance: Allows the method of appointing mayors and King's commissioners, for instance by election, to be changed by ordinary law without a further constitutional amendment.

description: Framework law for the irreversible, step-by-step reduction of Dutch greenhouse-gas emissions in line with the Paris Agreement, with a 2030 target of a 49% cut (later raised to 55%). First introduced in 2016 by Diederik Samsom (PvdA) and Jesse Klaver (GL); Jetten took over D66's co-sponsorship from Stientje van Veldhoven in 2018 and VVD and CDA joined as co-sponsors in June 2018. Adopted by the House 112–27 and by the Senate on 28 May 2019; published in the Staatsblad on 10 July 2019.
significance: The legal basis of Dutch climate policy, later amended by Jetten as minister to raise the 2030 target to 55%.

law_name: Initiative bill to anchor EU membership in the Constitution (Verhoeven and Jetten, 35.202)
description: Constitutional bill (first reading) introduced in 2019 by D66 MPs Kees Verhoeven and Jetten to enshrine Dutch membership of the European Union in the Constitution and lay down a procedure for any withdrawal. Rejected by the House of Representatives in 2021.
significance: Failed in the House of Representatives.

law_name: Minimum CO2 Price for Electricity Generation Act (Wet minimum CO2-prijs elektriciteitsopwekking, 35.216)
description: Introduces a national floor price for the CO2 emitted by power producers in the EU emissions-trading system, levied as an additional tax when the EU allowance price is lower. Introduced in 2019; Jetten, with State Secretary Van Rij, brought it into the Staatsblad in 2022 (Stb. 2022, 132).
significance: Gives power producers a predictable minimum carbon price.

law_name: Amendment of the Climate Act implementing the European Climate Law (36.169)
description: Raises the Dutch 2030 target from a 49% to a 55% cut in greenhouse-gas emissions and makes climate neutrality by 2050 binding, in line with the European Climate Law (Stb. 2023, 271).
significance: Aligns Dutch law with the EU's 'Fit for 55' targets.

law_name: Temporary Climate Fund Act (Tijdelijke wet Klimaatfonds, 36.274)
description: Sets up the Climate Fund as a budget fund managed by the Minister for Climate and Energy, to finance measures by citizens, businesses and organisations that cut greenhouse-gas emissions (Stb. 2024, 16).
significance: Main financing instrument of the energy transition under Rutte IV.

law_name: Climate policy programme (2022) and additional climate package (2023)
description: Jetten's 2022 climate policy programme set out subsidies (insulation, renewable energy, electric cars), standards (such as a hybrid heat pump requirement from 2026 and solar panels on large roofs from 2025) and pricing (a tighter industrial CO2 levy, a higher air passenger tax) for five sectors to reach at least 55% less CO2 in 2030; an additional package followed in 2023. As minister he also designated new offshore wind zones to reach about 21 GW by around 2030 and named Borssele as preferred site for two new nuclear plants.
significance: Defined Dutch climate policy under the fourth Rutte cabinet.

law_name: Municipal Instruments for the Heat Transition Act (Wet gemeentelijke instrumenten warmtetransitie, 36.387)
description: Bill introduced with Housing Minister Hugo de Jonge in 2023 that lets municipalities set local rules for moving neighbourhoods off natural gas. Adopted by the House in April 2024 and enacted in 2024.
significance: Gives municipalities legal tools to phase out natural gas in the built environment.

law_name: Phase-out of net metering for small solar producers (afbouw salderingsregeling, 35.594)
description: Bill to phase out gradually the scheme that lets households offset solar power fed into the grid against power consumed. Adopted by the House in February 2023 but rejected by the Senate in 2024, with Jetten as the minister defending it.
significance: A defeat for Jetten in the Senate.

description: Submitted by Jetten as Minister for Climate and Energy in June 2024: strengthens public control over district-heating companies and large heat networks, consumer protection and price regulation of heat. Adopted by the House in July 2025 and by the Senate in December 2025.
significance: Framework for the expansion of district heating with a leading role for public companies.

description: Amends the Aliens Act 2000 to distinguish between refugee status and subsidiary protection and to tighten family reunification, especially for those with subsidiary protection. Introduced by the Schoof cabinet in 2025 (D66 voted against it in the House) and defended in the Senate by the Jetten cabinet's Asylum Minister Van den Brink; adopted by the Senate on 21 April 2026 (41–34), the same day it rejected the Asylum Emergency Measures Act. Published in the Staatsblad in June 2026.
significance: The main asylum law enacted under Jetten; the Senate also approved the implementation act for the EU Asylum and Migration Pact on 26 May 2026.

description: €20 billion package presented on 26 June 2026: farm-level emission norms for 2035, additional zones around about 100 vulnerable nature areas with €9 billion of support for farmers, €2.2 billion for nature restoration, a 50% nitrogen cut for industry and mobility by 2035 and a legally robust de minimis threshold so that projects with very small nitrogen deposition no longer need a permit. The bill with sector targets was due in the House in October 2026.
significance: Intended to restart permits for farming, housing, energy and infrastructure held up by the nitrogen problem; needs majorities in both chambers.

law_name: Budget Memorandum and Tax Plan 2027 (Miljoenennota and Belastingplan 2027), with the box 3 amending bill
description: First budget of the Jetten cabinet (15 September 2026): deficit of 2.9% of GDP in 2027 falling to 2.2% in 2030, investment in infrastructure, housing associations and CO2 storage, extended fuel-excise discount, abolition of the care-cost deduction from 2028, and the dropping of the AOW life-expectancy link and benefit cuts. On 2 October 2026 the cabinet added an amending bill (novelle) moving box 3 towards a capital-gains tax and more money for purchasing power. Votes in the House were scheduled for 12 November 2026.
significance: Pending: the minority cabinet still needed opposition support in both chambers as of October 2026.
